item: Rinse the rice and start it cooking (1½ cups rice to 2¼ cups water, simmer covered 18 minutes, then rest 5).
Sauce: whisk the soy sauce, brown sugar, honey, minced garlic, ginger and ¼ cup water. In a small cup, mix the cornstarch with 1 tbsp cold water.
Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces. Cut the broccoli into florets, the pepper into strips and the carrots into thin coins.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan over medium-high. Cook the chicken 6–7 minutes, stirring, until browned and cooked through (165°F). Move it to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil, then the carrots for 2 minutes, then the broccoli and pepper with a splash of water for 3–4 more minutes until crisp-tender.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce and bring to a simmer. Stir in the cornstarch mix and cook 1 minute until glossy and thick.
Leftovers pack well for work-day lunches. Keeps 3–4 days in the fridge.
Put a big pot of well-salted water on to boil. Heat the oven to 400°F for the bread.
Dice the onion and mince 4 cloves of garlic. Warm the olive oil in a saucepan over medium and cook the onion 5 minutes until soft, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, basil, oregano, pepper flakes and ½ tsp salt. Simmer uncovered 15–20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Garlic bread: soften the butter and mix in the last 2 cloves of garlic, minced. Split the loaf lengthwise, spread with the butter and bake 10–12 minutes until golden at the edges.
Cook the spaghetti 1 minute short of the package time. Save ½ cup pasta water, then drain.
Toss the spaghetti in the sauce with a splash of pasta water. Serve with parmesan and the garlic bread.
The sauce freezes well. Make a double batch and freeze half for an easy off-day dinner.
Take the steak out of the fridge 30 minutes early. Pat it dry and season well with salt and pepper.
Fries: heat the oven to 425°F. Cut the potatoes into ½-inch sticks, soak 10 minutes in cold water, then dry well. Toss with 2 tbsp oil, salt and garlic powder.
Spread the fries in one layer on a sheet pan and bake 30–35 minutes, flipping halfway, until crisp and golden.
With 10 minutes left on the fries, heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy skillet over high until it just smokes. Sear the steak 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare (130°F).
Lower the heat, add the butter and crushed garlic, and spoon the butter over the steak for 30 seconds. Rest it on a board 5–8 minutes.
Steam the broccoli florets over 1 inch of boiling water, covered, 4–5 minutes until bright green and tender. Season with salt.
Slice the steak against the grain and serve with the fries and broccoli.
